Landing the thrown Bakugan on that Gate card requires a touchscreen flick/steer gesture (per the in-game Alice tutorial text: "make short strokes on the Touch Screen with the stylus after you throw"). Roughly 20 distinct synthetic-input techniques were tried against this gesture through the toolkit's X11 host driver (varying drag duration from 20ms to smooth 350ms interpolations, step counts from 2 to 30, dwell time at the release point, chained single-invocation xdotool mousedown/mousemove/mouseup, direction and distance, long holds up to 3.6s, and the on-screen confirm icon), and in every case the throw did not register: the ball visibly tracks the stylus 1:1 while held (proving touch delivery and coordinate mapping are correct, consistent with the same mapping working for every other confirmed interaction: grid-cell selection, the Bakugan-select OK button, and the Gate Card peek icon) but snaps back to the ready pose within one frame of release rather than launching. This looks like a synthetic-input fidelity limit of the sandboxed X11 driver against this specific gesture recognizer, not a toolkit defect: the reliability layer itself (launch, debugger_reachable, window health, watchdog, scenario execution with a live PC snapshot) was independently exercised successfully in the same session. No checkpoint in describe_required_checkpoints() has been captured, and no Timing* breakpoint has fired against a real session as a result.
